notes: The underlying model already does a strong job at finding pain points even without the skill -- the biggest, most consistent gap is structural: the skill enforces the five-bucket cybersecurity taxonomy and a confidence rating per pain point, while baseline runs use ad hoc headers and narrative framing instead.

Baseline runs in all three evals added an unrequested sales-recommendation section (e.g. 'Recommended focus for your follow-up', 'Recommended opening angle') even though none of the prompts asked for next steps -- this is scope creep the skill explicitly avoids.

Eval 3 (cross-call comparison) shows the smallest gap (0.8 vs 1.0) -- the comparison structure itself seems to nudge the baseline model toward the same recurring/new/escalated framing even without the skill, since the prompt itself asks for that structure explicitly.

With-skill runs consistently took longer and used more tokens (~18s, ~4900 tokens more on average) -- worth knowing this is not a free win, it trades some latency/cost for consistency and taxonomy adherence.
